Root question: Do more members of a machine-learned weather ensemble buy better forecasts of rare extremes, or does error shared by all members cap the skill?
Option record: {\"id\":\"ml-ensemble-extremes\",\"title\":\"Ensemble size for rare extremes in a machine-learned weather ensemble\",\"summary\":\"ECMWF runs its machine-learned ensemble, AIFS-ENS, operationally with 50 members, and the model weights are public. An extra member needs one GPU run rather than a supercomputer slot, so ensembles of hundreds or thousands look affordable. Study whether 10 to 1,000 members improve probability forecasts of rare extremes, such as top-percentile wind, temperature or rainfall. Score against ERA5 reanalysis and station observations, which the model did not produce. The open question is whether more members keep helping or whether error shared by every member caps the skill.\",\"root_link\":\"SAME: the director's C1 question made concrete on one open, operational model.\",\"compute_open\":\"Ensemble members per forecast, from about 10 to 1,000. Unknown: whether skill on top-percentile events keeps rising past the operational 50 members, or flattens because members share model error. The closest prior, HENS, ran 7,424 members of a different model (SFNO) for summer 2023.\",\"sequential\":\"not given\",\"source_urls\":[\"https://huggingface.co/ecmwf/aifs-ens-1.0\",\"https://forum.ecmwf.int/t/inference-with-aifs-ens-v-1-on-s2s-timescales/14832\",\"https://meetingorganizer.copernicus.org/EMS2026/EMS2026-212.html\",\"https://eesm.science.energy.gov/sites/default/files/Fri_Mahesh_HugeEnsembles.pdf\"]}
Card:
card:question: Does 10 to 1,000 AIFS-ENS members beat 50 for top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain probability forecasts, or does shared model error cap the skill?
card:hypothesis: More members keep helping: 1,000 members sample top-percentile tails far better than 50, so extreme-event scores keep improving [s_hens].
card:sequential_part: Each member's 60 six-hour autoregressive steps; 7,000 members across 7 dates.
card:method: none
card:if_lever: Skill on top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain keeps rising past 50 members: 1,000 members sharpen the tails and improve extreme-event scores.
card:if_not: Skill flattens near 50 members: members are exchangeable draws of one trained distribution, so shared model error caps tail sharpness and extra members add nothing.
card:test_summary: Run 7,000 fifteen-day AIFS-ENS v1 forecasts (7 dates x 1,000 members) on eight A100 40 GB GPUs; subsample 10-1,000 members, score top-percentile wind/temperature/rain probabilities against ERA5 with fair CRPS and Brier scores, and test whether skill still rises past 50 members.
card:closest_prior: HENS Part 2: 7,424 SFNO members per day for 92 summer-2023 dates; showed huge ensembles sample 4-sigma tails and reduce outliers.
card:left_open: Whether AIFS-ENS, whose members are exchangeable draws of one afCRPS-trained distribution, keeps gaining skill past 50 members or saturates from shared model error.
card:anchor: Reproduce the published 4-minute N320 member time and 38 GB memory; one control run must match ECMWF open data within ensemble spread [s_crps_paper].
card:limits: Applies to AIFS-ENS v1 medium-range extremes on 7 dates; not a multi-season reforecast, other models, subseasonal leads, or direct proof that shared error causes any saturation.

Criteria:
stakes: Take the two outcomes this test predicts, as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap. 5 = whichever occurs, a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) changes, and the test measures the quantity that choice depends on; 3 = the outcomes bear on that choice only through a step this test does not check (a stand-in system, simulation to reality, a single model), or one outcome is already much more likely than the other; 1 = neither outcome would change anything. Do not score how famous the field is or how close it is to the root question.
lever: Could the result tell if_lever from if_not, with compute the only thing that changed? Check four conditions: (a) the predicted difference between if_lever and if_not is larger than what noise_rule says run-to-run noise can produce; (b) compute_axis spans at least 10×; (c) the varied quantity is bought with compute, not with more data, labels or people (when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on the same hardware and differ only in method); (d) inputs that could also explain the difference are in held_fixed. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail, or the measured quantity is not the one the question asks about.
verifiable: What is the measured outcome scored against? 5 = an exact or planted truth that does not come from the method under test (a simulation's hidden true run, an exact success flag, a formal checker, planted items), and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance; 3 = labels from a model or human rater with an agreement check, or exact truth with no reproduction step; 1 = nothing independent of the method's own output.
open: Does the closest published result already answer this question over this range? 5 = the quoted prior stops short of this range or asks a different question, and the plan states the gap; 3 = the prior answers part of it (a narrower range, a related system), or no prior is named; 1 = the quoted prior already answers it. Reusing published tools, models or benchmarks does not lower this score.
reshape: Does the plan remove a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on, rather than run independent work side by side? 5 = restructuring names the dependency, why it need not run in order and how the plan computes it at the same time; condition says what must hold for that to pay off; condition_phase measures it before the main spend; and the closest prior does not already do this for this system; 3 = it removes a dependency, but condition is missing or is not measured before the main spend; 2 = it parallelises only within each step (splitting a large state across GPUs) or regroups and rebalances independent work (batching unfinished runs, load balancing, lower precision), leaving the chain in order; 1 = independent copies side by side, or one job per GPU, is the only parallelism, or the plan rebuilds a parallel version the closest prior already reports for this system. Reusing a method published for a different system does not lower this score.
baseline: Is the gain timed against the strongest ways to get the same answer without the plan's method? Check four conditions: (a) baseline_sequential is tuned (compiled, vectorised or multithreaded code, or a published optimised code), not a plain interpreted loop; (b) baseline_copies is timed on the same GPUs; (c) anchor checks the parallel result against the sequential one within a stated tolerance; (d) a named phase times every arm as time or dollars to one answer, so the gain is measured, not only modelled. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail. NA when restructuring.method is none.

Let me score each criterion.

Stakes: The question — does more members help or does shared error cap skill — directly affects whether ECMWF should buy more GPUs to run more members operationally. If skill keeps rising, buy compute; if it caps, don't. But limits: only 7 dates, one model, ERA5. The criteria say "as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap" — within7 dates on one model, a decision to scale to thousands of members depends on multi-season generality. That's a step not checked. But the two outcomes as measured: either skill rises past 50 or flat. If flat on 7 dates, do you stop planning huge ensembles? Somewhat. I'd say 4 — outcomes bear on buy-compute choice but through single-model/single-window step. Actually the criterion 5 requires "the test measures the quantity that choice depends on" — it does measure skill vs member count. But within limits, generality to multi-season not checked. I'll give 4.

Lever: (a) predicted difference: decision_rule says if_lever requires >= 0.01 gain and still rising; if_not < 0.005 flat within bootstrap CI. Is that larger than noise? Noise rule: bootstrap over members and 7 dates, 95% paired CI. 7 dates is few; a 0.01 Brier difference over 7 dates could be within noise. Cannot be told — plausibly marginal. (b) compute axis 10 to 1000 = 100×, passes. (c) quantity bought with compute — members, yes, passes. (d) held_fixed covers model, leads, variables, scoring, dates — passes. So (a) questionable: one condition fails or cannot be told → 3. Actually the thresholds0.01 vs 0.005 are close together, and the gap between decision thresholds could be produced by noise over 7 dates. I'd say 3.

Verifiable: Scored against ERA5 reanalysis, independent of the model, plus station observations. Anchor reproduces published 4-min member time and control run matches ECMWF open data within spread. Exact truth (reanalysis) + reproduction step → 5. Though ERA5 is itself a model-based reanalysis, but it's independent truth not from method under test. And anchor exists. 5.

Open: HENS ran 7,424 SFNO members for summer 2023, showed huge ensembles sample tails — but on a different model (SFNO), and the plan states the gap (AIFS-ENS exchangeable draws, saturating?). The prior stops short / different system and gap is stated → 5. Though HENS did measure skill saturation? HENS Part 2 showed sampling of 4-sigma tails and reduced outliers, arguably answers part. But different model, and question is about shared-error cap. Plan states left_open. 5.

Reshape: restructuring.method = "none", sequential_part just names member rollout steps. No dependency removal claimed. 1. Wait — could subsampling from one 1,000-member run to get all arm sizes count? That's regrouping independent work? The reshape criterion: plan doesn't claim restructuring; method is none. The subsampling design means one big run gives all levels — but that's not removing a step-after-step dependency.1.

Baseline: restructuring.method is none → NA.

Decides_by: The earliest phase after which decision_rule can be applied whichever outcome. p_score computes fair CRPS/Brier vs N with bootstrap — that's when the decision rule applies. p_main only generates forecasts. So decides_by = p_score.

Check: p_score subsamples and computes scores vs N with bootstrap CIs — yes, decision_rule applied there. p_station is stretch verification, not needed. So p_score.

Reasons within 25 words.
